speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment what is being done to mitigate against the various chemical odours/fumes (besides cocoa) emanating from the factories in Pioneer constituency that adversely impact the households located within their close proximity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This PSI is comparable to the rest of Singapore during the same period which ranges from 14 to 76.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA has in place a suite of measures to manage emissions from industrial premises, including factories in Pioneer Constituency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Factories are required to install pollution control equipment to ensure that their emissions are properly treated before discharge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Industries with processes that emit higher levels of air pollutants are required to engage accredited surveyors to conduct source emission testing and submit the test reports to NEA regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA also conducts regular factory inspections to verify that their pollution control equipment is well maintained and operating effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Some factories in the Jurong Industrial Estate, such as those specialising in the manufacturing of food flavourings and fragrances, generate certain smells during their operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Such smells are generally not harmful to human health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA will continue to ensure that industries meet air emission standards and will enforce against companies found to be non-compliant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: My Ministry also regularly reviews the industrial emission standards to ensure they are on par with those in other jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Just wanted to share because, just last night, in fact, two residents buzzed me through private message to share about chemical smells and odours coming from the nearby factory areas, mainly, Soon Lee as well as further down, near Boon Lay Way.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Essentially, the smells come partly exacerbated by the fact of strong winds and wind directions, so I just wanted to give a few suggestions to Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Second, whether we can do environmental audits in a more regular fashion for those industries which particularly have emissions of smoke, fumes as well as other odours.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Thirdly, whether NEA can work more closely with the community to be a bit more proactive, as and when we detect some of these cases to engage those companies and businesses in the area.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me thank the Member for his suggestions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, we have continuous, real-time air monitoring sensors, a network of these sensors that will measure Pollutant Standards Index as well as VOCs, to ensure that the ambient air quality is within the range of good to moderate and that the VOC levels are within the safe levels.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But I must caveat that we cannot guarantee; we will do our best.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Also, allow me to clarify that every time when a smell incident is reported, if it is distinctive and we can trace it to a specific factory, we will engage the factory and advise them to implement smell mitigation measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the years, quite a number of these factories have been implementing or have implemented smell mitigation measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, scrubbers, odour control systems, dispersion fans and to the extent that some of them will also moderate their operations, in order to mitigate the smells.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And as the Member has rightly pointed out, particularly during the months from April to November, due to the Southwest monsoon as well as the inter-monsoon period, sometimes the wind will carry over these smells or the smells could linger because of lack of variability in the wind speed and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, as I have said, for the smell incidents that have been reported thus far, we have not found elevated levels of ambient air pollutant indicators, which means that they are within safe levels.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to proactively respond to such reports of smell incidents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the lower risk factories, it is once a year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, there are actually measures that we put in place to mitigate this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we will continue to see what we can do.
